title: Individual principal-support Kummer boundary
statement: Fix the finite-field and positive finite coefficient datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], with ring $A$. Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Put $i:D=V(f)\hookrightarrow X$, the principal zero closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:W=X_f\hookrightarrow X$ be its complementary open [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its restricted function is the actual localization unit. Use the finite root-tensor twist $A(1)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and the all-level Kummer class of [def-pur-frame-kummer-class], on the site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Define the individual supported boundary $\alpha_X(f)\in H^2_D(X,A(1))$ [def-pur-support-cohomology] by applying the closed-open support connecting map of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to $\kappa_W(f|_W)$. In the supported-Hom convention of [def-pur-supported-cup], this is composition with the canonical coefficient extension $0\to j_!A_W\to A_X\to i_*A_D\to0$: apply exact $j_!$ to the Kummer extension, map its target to $A(1)_X$ by the counit through the normalized twist restriction, then compose its degree-one Ext class with the coefficient extension class and take its derived-Hom representative. The coefficient maps are extension by zero followed by the counit and restriction of locally constant functions. This defines the class for every function, including a unit, a zero function, and the empty scheme; it does not assert Cartier or non-zero-divisor hypotheses.
